content_sanskrit: पुरोपकण्ठसंप्राप्तैश्चतुर्दिक्कं सहारिभिः । एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र प्रवृत्तं दारुणं रणम्
padaccheda: पुर-उपकण्ठ-संप्राप्तैः । चतुर्दिक्कं । सह । अरिभिः । एतस्मिन् । अन्तरे । तत्र । प्रवृत्तं । दारुणं । रणम्
anvaya: एतस्मिन् अन्तरे तत्र पुर-उपकण्ठ-संप्राप्तैः अरिभिः सह चतुर्दिक्कं दारुणं रणं प्रवृत्तम्
meaning_english: In the meantime, a fierce battle commenced there in all four directions, involving enemies who had arrived at the outskirts of the city.
The battle resulted in the plundering of villages and towns, leaving the masses of people in great distress; it was filled with bodies burning in fire and enveloped by thick clouds of smoke.
The sun was concealed by the great smoke and nets of arrows, causing darkness to prevail; one moment the sun was visible, and the next, the solar disc vanished from sight.
The heat from the blazing fires scorched the leafy forests, while the sky became filled with swaying firebrands, spears, clubs, and stones.
The weapons seemed to burn with double intensity due to the reflections of the fire; meanwhile, the great heroes fallen in battle attained the nectar-like company of the celestial damsels of Indra.
The trumpeting of wild elephants delighted those eager for combat, as the battlefield rained down bhuśuṇḍī missiles, discs, spears, and lances.
The roar of the soldiers caused the hearts of the weak to fail, leading to their death, while the mass of dust acted like white clouds, blocking the path to heaven.

padaccheda: मरण-व्यग्र-सामन्त-मुक्त-नाद-व्रजत्-रजम् । इतः । च । इतः । च । निपतत्-वैद्युत-उपहत-प्रजम्
anvaya: (तत् रणं) मरण-व्यग्र-सामन्त-मुक्त-नाद-व्रजत्-रजम् इतः च इतः च निपतत्-वैद्युत-उपहत-प्रजम् (आसीत्)
meaning_english: Dust rose as the chieftains, intent on death, let out cries, while the people were struck down by lightning-like weapons falling from all sides.
Falling houses burnt by fire released clouds of flame, and the sky was filled with clouds consisting of countless showers of arrows that granted the joy of death to the warriors.
The galloping horses surpassed the waves of the ocean, and the air was harsh with the high-pitched clashing sounds produced by the tusks of elephants colliding.

anvaya: कोट-कोटि-कुटी-कुड्य-कण्टक-उद्भट-सद्-भटम् (यथा स्यात् तथा) चठत्-कुण्ठित-कोट-अट्ट-कृट-अटन-नटत्-छटम् (तत् युद्धम् अभवत्) ।
meaning_english: The battle raged with excellent soldiers appearing like thorns upon the walls of millions of fortresses, while the dancing mass of luster flickered as they moved through the peaks of the blunted battlements.
The conflict featured clearly visible spears amidst the fierce striking of falling garments, while the sky was filled with the flapping 'paṭa-paṭa' sounds of cloth banners twisting around the towers.

anvaya: दन्ति-दन्त-गुण-उद्गीर्णैः हेति-पाषाण-घर्षणैः तार-क्रेंकार-हुंकारैः आहूत-सुर-वारणम् (तत् युद्धम् अभवत्) ।
meaning_english: Through the friction of weapons and stones, and the sounds emitted from the bowstrings made of elephant-hide, the high-pitched 'kreṃ' and 'huṃ' cries seemed to summon the divine elephants of the gods.
The great ocean of the sky was filled by the flooding rivers of flying arrows, made harsh by the 'makara' sea-monsters in the form of moving discs, spears, and the edges of swords.
The circle of islands seemed formed by the ringing 'jhaṇajhaṇā' sounds and the fierce clanging of armor during the collision of shouting warriors.
A mire was created by arrows crushed under the trampling of feet, while chariots and elephants were swept away by the speed of the flowing rivers of blood.
Broad-bladed spears fell and rose with the ease of Garuda, while broken weapons appeared like distressed aquatic creatures caught in the waves of the water-like arrows.
The sky was set ablaze by flames emerging from the clash of weapons, as the heavens were invaded by brave warriors who had liberated themselves from wrinkles and gray hair through death in battle.
The flashes of discs shone like lightning within clouds of pale dust, while the earth became the support for those fighting in a sky rendered solid by the density of weapons.
The battle grew intense with the roaring of opposing soldiers and the pride of warriors, as chariots rolled amidst the wood crushed by the collision of crashing carts.
The battlefield was crowded with a thorny thicket composed of headless trunks, soldiers, and vampires. It featured the lotus-hearts of the flesh of the finest corpses being devoured by Vetālas.

The field was strewn with half-severed heads, hands, hooves, and thighs cut down by heroes. The sky was transformed into a quivering forest by the tree-like arms of headless trunks dancing in the air.
The groups of Vetālas clattered their teeth in laughter with restless, gaping mouths. The scene was terrifying with the frowns of soldiers clad in fierce armor and displaying intense pride.
The battle was adorned exclusively by incessant killing and dying. It was filled with the boundless defect of misery arising from the giving and receiving of violent blows.
The conflict dried up the rut-fluid of the elephants of heroic lords. It nourished the joy of Yama, the God of Death, who finds exclusive delight in the act of killing.

content_sanskrit: अविकत्थनगुप्तानां शूराणां जयघोषणम् । अशूराणां च गुप्तानां प्रभावुद्धोषणं परम्
padaccheda: अविकत्थनगुप्तानाम् । शूराणाम् । जयघोषणम् । अशूराणाम् । च । गुप्तानाम् । प्रभावुद्धोषणम् । परम्
anvaya: (तत् युद्धम्) अविकत्थन-गुप्तानाम् शूराणाम् जय-घोषणम् (आसीत्), अ-शूराणाम् च गुप्तानाम् प्रभा-उद्धोषणम् परम् (आसीत्)।
meaning_english: The war proclaimed the victory of heroes who were modest and hidden, while it also served as the supreme announcer of the true nature and brilliance of those who were secretly cowards.

content_sanskrit: शौर्यादीनां प्रसुप्तानां स्वगुणानां प्रबोधनम् । धनमाधारभूतानां राष्ट्रेषु भुजशालिनाम्
padaccheda: शौर्यादीनाम् । प्रसुप्तानाम् । स्वगुणानाम् । प्रबोधनम् । धनम् । आधारभूतानाम् । राष्ट्रेषु । भुजशालिनाम्
anvaya: (तत् युद्धम्) प्रसुप्तानाम् शौर्य-आदीनाम् स्व-गुणानाम् प्रबोधनम् (आसीत्), राष्ट्रेषु भुज-शालिनाम् आधार-भूतानाम् धनम् (आसीत्)।
meaning_english: The battle served as an awakening for dormant virtues like heroism. It was the true wealth for the strong-armed men who are the foundational pillars of their kingdoms.
Warriors mounted on elephants and chariots broke the temples of rival elephants with their impacts. The battle checked the flow of rut-water from all the intoxicated, scent-trailing elephants.
The battlefield was filled with intoxicated elephants released by powerful, shouting chieftains. It caused the pain of sword-strikes inflicted by armies that had conquered even the fatigue of age.

content_sanskrit: दिनं दिनकरस्येव नृपस्य शरणं गतम् । अनागतभटव्रातपिष्टार्धमृतमानवम्
padaccheda: दिनम् । दिनकरस्य । इव । नृपस्य । शरणम् । गतम् । अनागतभटव्रातपिष्टार्धमृतमानवम्
anvaya: (तत् युद्धम्) दिनकरस्य दिनम् इव नृपस्य शरणम् गतम् (आसीत्), अनागत-भट-व्रात-पिष्ट-अर्ध-मृत-मानवम् (च आसीत्)।
meaning_english: The battle sought the king's protection just as a day belongs to the Sun. It was a place where half-dead men were crushed by the advancing swarms of incoming soldiers.

anvaya: (तत् युद्धम्) मान-आयु-बल-उन्मत्त-नत-प्रारब्ध-कुट्टनम् (आसीत्), प्राण-पण्यानां धनानां नवम् आपण-पत्तनम् (च आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: The battle was a place where those intoxicated by pride, youth, and strength began a subduing slaughter; it served as a new market-town for the exchange of lives as the currency for wealth.

anvaya: (तत् युद्धम्) पट-नद्ध-पताक-ओघ-जात-संचारि-दोः-द्रुमम्, रक्त-उज्ज्वलत्वात् त्रैलोक्य-लक्ष्म्याः भूषण-विद्रुमम् (इव आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: With moving tree-like arms draped in clusters of banners, the battlefield resembled the coral ornament of the Fortune of the three worlds due to its brilliant blood-red hue.
The courtyard of the sky was filled with flowers of weaponry and covered by white umbrellas as beautiful as the milk-ocean waters churned by Mount Mandara.
The intentions of heroes were sung by the Gaṇas, gods, and Gandharvas; the battlefield was filled with Hālāhala poison-like weapons, their tips flickering like palm leaves in the light.
The battle resounded with the clanging of numerous weapons wielded by hosts of Yātudhānas, having consumed the strange, evil trees that filled the mountain-cave dwellings.
The sky was covered by severed heads and hands tossed within a forest of shining spears, while the creepers of the cardinal directions were flooded by torrents of stones flung from slings.
Great trees were bursting and melting with loud crackling sounds, and the city dwellings echoed with the tumultuous wailing of women.

anvaya: मन्दर-आवानल-आकार-नभः-भात-आयुध-व्रजम् (युद्धं दृष्ट्वा), धनं गेहं (च) परित्यज्य प्रजाः दूर-उर्वी-विद्रुत-प्रजम् (अभवन्) ।
meaning_english: Seeing the mass of weapons shining in the sky like the submarine fire of Mandara, the subjects abandoned their wealth and homes and fled to distant lands.

padaccheda: सर्वतोहेतिवहनात् । समक्षप्रेक्षकोज्झितम् । वर्जितम् । भीरुभिः । पक्षिराजवृन्दम् । इव । अहिभिः
anvaya: सर्वतः हेति-वहनात् समक्ष-प्रेक्षक-उज्झितम्, अहिभिः पक्षि-राज-वृन्दम् इव भीरुभिः वर्जितम् (तत् युद्धम् आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: Because it carried weapons everywhere, the battlefield was abandoned by onlookers; the timid avoided it just as serpents avoid a flock of Garuḍas.
The battlefield was crowded with noble warriors crushed by the tusks of elephants, resembling a wine-press of human grapes in the mat of Death.
The battle was one where weapons moving in the sky were crushed by the impact of stones from machines; it was filled with caves echoing with the roars of elephant herds and the shouts of warriors.

anvaya: धरा-धर-दरी-अन्तः-प्रतिश्रुत्-प्रोत-गर्जितम्, अर्जितम् प्राण-सर्वस्वम् अर्जयद्भिः उपार्जितम् (तत् युद्धम् आसीत्)।
meaning_english: The roars of the conflict were woven into echoes within mountain caves. This battle was fought by those who had already earned the ultimate wealth of life through their great deeds.

padaccheda: भर्जितम् । हेतिदहनैः । अग्निदाहैः । च । संततैः । तैः । एव । अन्यैः । अथ । अन्यैः । च । द्वन्द्वयुद्धैः । अनिष्ठितम्
anvaya: हेति-दहनैः (च) संततैः अग्नि-दाहैः भर्जितम्, तैः एव अन्यैः अथ अन्यैः च द्वन्द्व-युद्धैः अनिष्टितम् (तत् युद्धम् आसीत्)।
meaning_english: The battlefield was scorched by the fires of weapons and continuous flames; it was ceaselessly engaged in duels by those very warriors and many others.

content_sanskrit: वेष्टितं मृतशिष्टैश्च सारैः सुभटपेटकैः । कैलासैरिव संशुद्धैरीश्वराधारतां गतैः
padaccheda: वेष्टितम् । मृतशिष्टैः । च । सारैः । सुभटपेटकैः । कैलासैः । इव । संशुद्धैः । ईश्वराधारताम् । गतैः
anvaya: मृत-शिष्टैः सारैः सुभट-पेटकैः वेष्टितम्, संशुद्धैः ईश्वर-आधारताम् गतैः कैलासैः इव (तत् युद्धम् आसीत्)।
meaning_english: Surrounded by the remaining elite circles of great warriors, the battlefield appeared like the pure peaks of Mount Kailāsa which serve as the abode of the Lord Īśvara.

content_sanskrit: तैरुदारैः समाक्रान्तं ये मृत्योरपि मृत्यवः । मरणं जीवितं येषां जीवितं मरणं रणे
padaccheda: तैः । उदारैः । समाक्रान्तम् । ये । मृत्योः । अपि । मृत्यवः । मरणम् । जीवितम् । येषाम् । जीवितम् । मरणम् । रणे
anvaya: ये मृत्योः अपि मृत्यवः, येषाम् रणे मरणम् जीवितम् (अस्ति), जीवितम् (च) मरणम् (अस्ति), तैः उदारैः (तत् युद्धम्) समाक्रान्तम्।
meaning_english: The battle was overrun by those noble heroes who are the very death of Death itself; for them, dying in battle is true living, and mere living is like death.

content_sanskrit: रणे नभसि निर्लूनवरवारणवारिजे । सारसाः सरसीवात्र रेजुरत्युद्भटा भटाः
padaccheda: रणे । नभसि । निर्लूनवरवारणवारिजे । सारसाः । सरसि । इव । अत्र । रेजुः । अत्युद्भटाः । भटाः
anvaya: रणे नभसि निर्लून-वर-वारण-वारिजे, अत्र सरसि सारसाः इव अति-उद्भटाः भटाः रेजुः।
meaning_english: In that sky-like battlefield, where the severed heads of great elephants were like lotuses, the fierce warriors shone like cranes in a lake.

content_sanskrit: यन्त्राश्मक्षेपणानां प्रसरणसरितां घूकृतैः फूत्कृतैर्द्राक् क्रान्तानां व्योम्नि मूर्ध्नां शरसलिलमुचां सैनिकानां च नादैः । टांकारैरायुधानां नभसि विसरतामश्वचक्रेभशब्दैरासीन्निःसंधिबन्धोपलजठरजडं जीर्णकर्णं गतं तत्
padaccheda: यन्त्राश्मक्षेपणानाम् । प्रसरणसरिताम् । घूकृतैः । फूत्कृतैः । द्राक् । क्रान्तानाम् । व्योम्नि । मूर्ध्नाम् । शरसलिलमुचाम् । सैनिकानाम् । च । नादैः । टांकारैः । आयुधानाम् । नभसि । विसरताम् । अश्वचक्रेभशब्दैः । आसीत् । निःसंधिबन्धोपलजठरजडम् । जीर्णकर्णम् । गतम् । तत्
anvaya: यन्त्र-अश्म-क्षेपणानाम् प्रसरण-सरिताम् घू-कृतैः, द्राक् क्रान्तानाम् फू-कृतैः, व्योम्नि मूर्ध्नाम् (च), शर-सलिल-मुचाम् सैनिकानाम् नादैः, नभसि विसरताम् आयुधानाम् टां-कारैः, अश्व-चक्र-इभ-शब्दैः (च) तत् (जगत्) निःसंधि-बन्ध-उपल-जठर-जडम् जीर्ण-कर्णम् गतम् आसीत्।
meaning_english: By the whirring of stone-throwing machines, the hissing of those suddenly attacked, the cries of soldiers releasing showers of arrows, the clashing of weapons in the sky, and the sounds of horses, chariots, and elephants, the entire world became as deaf as the interior of a solid stone.
